Name: Voice Over Framework Mod (VOFM) No Longer Maintained
Author: Darkmushu1
Description:
I'm quitting modding to explore other things in life, whoever wants to take over the project and or maintain just let me know and I can add a redirect link here to your Nexus mod page.

[b]What does this mod do?[/b]
This mod doesn't do anything by itself. This mod allows user to select a character voice from each voice packs. Once a voice pack is set, dialogues will play the audio from that voice pack.

[b]Platform Support[/b]
Works on PC / Android (mobile) /Linux (steam deck) / MacOS (should work on Mac OS but have not tested)

[b]Compatibility[/b]
Works with other voice over mod like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22550]Stardew Voices[/url], You just have to set the character voices in this voice pack to blank to play voices from other mods like this one.
Should work with other AI Voice Over like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/25024]Speaking valley[/url], but may need to set character voices to blank to play other voices.﻿

[b]How Do you create a voice pack?[/b]
[spoiler]
If you want to create them using AI through Elevenlabs here is the step using a script to generate all voices in your preferred languages (The example is for Spanish but you could generate the same template for other language by just setting game to a different language and choosing your language when creating template)
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/3994]Producing an AI Spanish Voice Pack instructions for user - FastWey at Stardew Valley Nexus - Mods and community[/url]

If you want to manually voice them or have a team voice them follow the steps below

[b]1.How to create voice packs for format 2.0.0 in version 1.0.6+?
[/b]
[spoiler]

If you want to manually create them by voicing it yourself or have other manual voice them follow these steps:
Here are steps to create your own voice pack.
1. Load into a save game. Once game is loaded. Type 'Help' to see all available commands for every mod including this one.
2. Go to SMAPI type 'help create_template' it'll show you what to type to get what character pack you want to create for in what language.
3. Enter the proper create_template like  "create_template all en Author.ModName 'Voice Pack Name' 1 ogg" which creates template for all characters in english.
4. A Folder is then created now you can open charactername_Language.json  file and see like this below, and DialogueText is what you need to voice over and then save it to the where that Audiopath is telling you to save it under and as that file name. 

          "DialogueFrom": "Introduction",
          "DialogueText": "Oh, that's right... I heard someone new was moving onto that old farm.",
          "AudioPath": "assets/en/Abigail/1.ogg",
          "TranslationKey": "Characters/Dialogue/Abigail:Introduction",
          "PageIndex": 0,
          "DisplayPattern": "Oh, that's right... I heard someone new was moving onto that old ."
        
In the DialogueText sometimes you'll see some weird symbols like %noun and in the game this would be replaced by a random noun in the game, %verb to a random Verb, @  to replace as to farmer and you can reference the rules and tokens that can display from the official wiki ( [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Dialogue#Algorithm]Modding:Dialogue - Stardew Valley Wiki[/url]).  I do try to expand some of these in brackets so your able to tell what the dialogue is doing example in event dialogue you might see {portrait: Happy} instead of $h so that you can just continue working without having to look these up in the wiki but if I do miss some the wiki is there. Things that will come up, random noun, verb, adjective, farmer name, farm's name, spouse name, 1st child name, 2nd child name, Sam's band name, Elliott's book name, random place, random word generator, and more.  

5. You should also include a manifest.json file with the content below but with your information.

{
  "Name": "NameOfYourVoicePack",
  "Author": "YourName",
  "Version": "1.0.0",
  "Description": "AddDiscription",
  "UniqueID": "YourName.NameOfYourVoicePack",
  "UpdateKeys": [ "Nexus:YourNexusIDGoesHERE" ],
  "ContentPackFor": {
    "UniqueID": "Darkmushu1.VoiceOverFrameworkMod"
  }
}

See video for Demo of how you can create your own voice pack leveraging the template creator. The video below is old for template 1 but should still work for our new template format 2.0.0 which uses the same command.
[youtube]fXB-8RU0jzc[/youtube][/spoiler]

[b]2.How to port no version format which defaults to format 1.0.0 to the new format 2.0.0?[/b]
[spoiler]
If you started a voice pack in VOFM in before version 1.0.6 and want to port to new version, you can use the command
"vof_port 'VoicePackFolderNameInModsFolder' ogg"  this will export all matching dialogue lines of V1.0.0 format and it's audio into Version 2.0.0 format and renames the audio accordingly for you. The ported new folder will be the same name as the original mod but concatenates 'output' to the end of the new folder. In the ported folder you'll find a report folder indicating which dialogue was not ported over that may require manual review before manually moving over.

If you do move audio file into new voice pack manually you'll have to rename the audio to what is listed in the new character_language.json voice pack as the audiopath will have a different file name than previous format.[/spoiler]

[b]How to Test my voice pack is working?[/b]
[spoiler]
To test your dialogues,  event dialogues, and speech bubbles Use the commands below. The output at the end will provide you a summary of how much dialogue matches  your voice pack, how many audio are missing and more.

[b]"test_dialogue All 5000"  [/b] this will play each dialogue in character/dialogue  the marriage dialogues /Engagement Dialogue and some festival lines that aren't event related every 5 seconds. Don't set 5000 to lower than 250 or some dialogue just get skips without getting counted properly.

[b]"test_events all 5000" [/b] this will play each event dialogue and festival events dialogues every 5 seconds. Don't set 5000 to lower than 250 or some dialogue just get skips without getting counted properly.

[b]"test_bubbles all 5000" [/b]this will play each event dialogue and festival events dialogues every 5 seconds. Don't set 5000 to lower than 250 or some dialogue just get skips without getting counted properly.[/spoiler]

[b]3.Replace Dialogue Text in voice pack json files[/b]
[spoiler]
Once you run the test_dialogue, or test_events, or test_bubbles it'll show the original game dialogue, the parsed dialogue text and if match was found or not. If the match is not found you can add that line and the parsed dialogue inside the voice or or the dialogue exists already but just need to be modify you can moddify the "DisplayPattern" text field to match what is showin the sanitized text, as the display patter field is what VOF uses to compare sanitized game dialogue against your voice pack to find a match. [/spoiler]
